task: Correct this short international registration email using the supplied UTC deadline and fixed offset. Make the local date rollover intelligible in about 50–85 words. There is one deadline, not an extra grace period for a different clock. Do not infer regional daylight-saving rules.
input: Registration closes on Friday 16 October 2026 at 11:30 p.m. UTC. Readers using UTC+09:00 may register until 8:30 a.m. on Saturday 17 October, giving them an extra day. Use the lecture form before your local deadline.

facts.text: The fictional lecture's deadline is Thursday 15 October 2026 at 23:30 UTC.
For a clock fixed at UTC+09:00, the same instant is Friday 16 October 2026 at 08:30.
The two displayed times describe one deadline with no additional grace period.
Registrations must reach the form at https://example.org/lecture/signup by that deadline.

forbidden_additions: The incorrect Friday UTC or Saturday UTC+09:00 date.
An extra day or separate deadline for a different time zone.
Regional daylight-saving assumptions or a promised late-registration exception.
preserve: A single instant represented on two explicitly identified clocks.
The calendar-day rollover and the reserved-domain form URL.
A clear action before the deadline.
